additions.name: The Shop
additions.note: Resale shop on Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park selling donated clothing, accessories, and household goods, with proceeds supporting the Junior League of Palo Alto-Mid Peninsula. The Shop was established in 1970 and operates at 725 Santa Cruz Avenue.

additions.name: Afterwards
additions.note: Designer consignment shop selling women's clothing, handbags, shoes, furnishings and artwork in downtown Menlo Park. It opened in September 1990 and remains open.

additions.name: Menlo Park Academy of Dance
additions.note: Dance studio in downtown Menlo Park. It began in 1947 at another El Camino Real address, moved to 1163 El Camino Real in 1949, took its current name in 1969, and remains open.

additions.name: Sultana
additions.note: Turkish and Mediterranean restaurant near El Camino Real and Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. A Palo Alto Online review published June 30, 2006 lists Sultana at 1149 El Camino Real, and a later restaurant guide gives its opening year as 2006.

additions.name: Oak + Violet
additions.note: Restaurant inside the Park James Hotel that opened for dinner on October 8, 2018. The hotel dining page still lists current dinner hours and reservations.

additions.name: Luminaire
additions.note: Modern furniture and design showroom on Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. A January 2022 Modern Luxury article announced the new Menlo Park showroom opening that spring, and Luminaire's current showroom page lists 870 Santa Cruz Ave.

additions.name: Guapas Mexican Grill
additions.note: A Menlo Park school newspaper article published in November 2023 reports that the restaurant opened its Menlo Park doors on September 20 after a South San Francisco opening that February. Current listings still show the Mexican restaurant operating at 515 El Camino Real.

additions.name: Hotel Lucent
additions.note: Boutique hotel at 727 El Camino Real in Menlo Park, created through a comprehensive renovation of an existing hotel. It was operating under the Hotel Lucent name by fall 2015, when guest reviews described newly renovated rooms, and its official site still lists the hotel at this address.

additions.name: Fey Restaurant
additions.note: Sichuan restaurant on El Camino Real in Menlo Park. A local profile says the Menlo Park location opened in 2012, and current dining listings still show it open at 1368 El Camino Real.

additions.name: Residence Inn Palo Alto Menlo Park
additions.note: Extended-stay Marriott hotel with 138 suites on Glenwood Avenue near downtown Menlo Park. It opened in spring 2015 and is still operating.

additions.name: FedEx Office
additions.note: Print and ship center on El Camino Real in Menlo Park. A June 1995 local column lists a Kinko's copy shop at this address, and FedEx still operates its print and ship center there.

additions.name: Menlo Park Fire District Station 6
additions.note: Downtown fire station first built on this site in 1953. The old building was torn down in late 2016 and replaced by a larger station, which crews moved into in June 2018 and which still serves downtown Menlo Park.

additions.name: Guy Plumbing and Heating
additions.note: A family-owned plumbing business with a showroom at 1265 El Camino Real in Menlo Park has operated in Menlo Park since 1948. It remains open at the same address.

additions.name: Sugar Shack
additions.note: Candy shop on Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. A 2019 student newspaper account says the Sugar Shack originally opened in 2007 and closed in 2014, and Palo Alto Online placed the shop at 816 Santa Cruz Ave before its closure.

additions.name: Una Mas Mexican Grill
additions.note: Mexican grill on Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. Palo Alto Online reported in December 2019 that the restaurant at 683 Santa Cruz Ave had closed after operating there since 1994.

additions.name: Ann's Coffee Shop
additions.note: Diner on Santa Cruz Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. The Menlo Park Historical Association says the coffee shop relocated to 772 Santa Cruz Avenue about 1962 and closed in 2021 after its building was sold.

additions.name: Golden Shears
additions.note: Barber shop opened by Louis Arenas in 1963. It closed on January 10, 2016, after 53 years in downtown Menlo Park.

additions.name: LB Steak
additions.note: Steakhouse at the corner of Santa Cruz Avenue and University Drive in downtown Menlo Park. Palo Alto Online reported the restaurant at 898 Santa Cruz Ave opened in July 2012 and closed in April 2018 after about six years.

additions.name: Left Bank Brasserie
additions.note: French brasserie that opened in 1998 as the Menlo Park branch of a restaurant founded in Larkspur. It closed in June 2026 when its parent company shut all of its Bay Area restaurants.

additions.name: First Church of Christ, Scientist
additions.note: Church on Ravenswood Avenue in Menlo Park. Its history page says the present site at 201 Ravenswood Avenue was acquired in 1957 and first services in the first building there were held in April 1958; its current site lists services at the same address.

additions.name: Foster's Freeze
additions.note: Soft-serve ice cream and hamburger stand on Oak Grove Avenue near El Camino Real in Menlo Park. The Menlo Park Historical Association says it first appears in Polk directories at 580 Oak Grove in 1950, and a student newspaper reported its closing in October 2015.

additions.name: Su Hong To Go
additions.note: Takeout Chinese restaurant on Menlo Avenue in downtown Menlo Park. Palo Alto Online reported it opened at 630 Menlo Ave in 1991 and that the Su Hong name ended there on September 30, 2015 when the restaurant changed hands and name.

additions.name: Gambardella's
additions.note: Italian restaurant across from the Menlo Park Caltrain station. A 2004 Palo Alto Online review says Gambardella's reopened in November 2003 in the Menlo Square building at 1165 Merrill St, and a 2014 article says it closed in December 2012.

additions.name: Bradley's Fine Diner
additions.note: American diner from chef Bradley Ogden, known as BFD, across from the Menlo Park Caltrain station. Palo Alto Online reported it opened in November 2014 and had closed as of January 1, 2017.

additions.name: Jan's Deli
additions.note: Small weekday lunch deli known for hot roast turkey sandwiches on Dutch crunch rolls. Reviews document it at this address in 2015 and 2016.

additions.name: Iberia Restaurant
additions.note: Spanish restaurant and tapas bar that relocated to Menlo Park in 2000. It left this address after the building was sold in 2015.

additions.name: Los Salonez
additions.note: Hair salon that local readers voted best in town several times in the 2000s; it was described as 13 years old in 2004. Its block at 1010-1026 Alma St was redeveloped as Alma Station after city review in 2015.

fields.note: Peet's second store, after the original in Berkeley, opened in 1971 at the corner of Santa Cruz Avenue and University Drive. It briefly closed after a nearby fire in March 2009 and reopened that month.
Pizza restaurant at the corner of El Camino Real and Menlo Avenue, opened in 2019 as a Mountain Mike's franchise in the former longtime Applewood Pizza space.
Japanese sushi restaurant that soft-opened in late July 2017 in the former Tokyo Subway space on Santa Cruz Avenue. Still open today.
Bedding and bath shop run by the San Francisco retailer Anthem, next door to its Anthem home store at 889 Santa Cruz Ave. Anthem says it opened in downtown Menlo Park around 2017.
Dry cleaners on Santa Cruz Avenue that first appears in the 1959 Polk's Directory, so it probably opened about 1958. Still open today.
Window coverings showroom run by Rebarts Interiors as a Hunter Douglas Gallery dealer. Its grand opening at this address was held in October 2019.
Optometry practice and eyewear shop on Santa Cruz Avenue, still open. Customer reviews show it was open by about 2021; the exact opening year isn't known.
French pastry shop and cafe that opened in early October 2015 in the former Sugar Shack space. It was still open in 2025, its tenth year.
Dry cleaners on Santa Cruz Avenue. State pressure-vessel records show it operating here by September 2019, and it is still open today.
Rug shop in the 775-777 Santa Cruz Ave building, which earlier held beauty salons. It moved here from Mountain View around 2020.
Spice shop that opened at 771 Santa Cruz Ave in late November 2008 as the chain's first Northern California store. It is still open today.

Bank branch in the building American Trust Company opened by 1959 on the former Sunshine Market site at Santa Cruz Ave and Chestnut St. It became Wells Fargo after the two banks merged in 1960 and is still open.
Eyewear shop and licensed optician on Santa Cruz Avenue, open since 1988 according to the shop's own history page. Still operating at this address.
Needlepoint shop selling hand-painted canvases and threads, with classes from beginner to advanced. It was holding classes by 2012 and may have opened earlier.
Goodwill's Menlo Park boutique thrift store, recorded here by early 2014 and possibly open earlier. It closed in January 2025 when its lease ended.
Exercise equipment showroom on Santa Cruz Avenue. The city's 2022 downtown market study listed it among new businesses that opened during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Bank of the West moved its Menlo Park branch here from 900 Santa Cruz Avenue in December 2010, according to state banking records. The branch became BMO in 2023 after BMO bought Bank of the West.
Coffee shop in the former Clifford's Pharmacy building on Santa Cruz Avenue. Local press reported it coming in early 1995, and permits for its signs and building work were issued that spring.
Listed as Park Avenue Salon and Galerie, a salon that also showed paintings, in Palo Alto Online gallery listings from 2001 and 2004. It is still open today, and it may have opened before 2001.
Nail salon offering manicures, pedicures and nail enhancements, still listed at 1020 Doyle St in current directories. The year it opened isn't known yet.
Optician and eyewear shop on University Drive, open today. Business directories list it at this address; the year it opened isn't known yet.
Coin and precious-metals dealer with a walk-in showroom on University Drive, documented there by 2014 and still listed today. It may have been there earlier, but no earlier year has been confirmed.
European-style counter-service cafe next to Kepler's Books, which the Borrone family moved here in 1989 after opening it in Redwood City in 1979. It is still open today.

American Cancer Society resale shop selling donated clothing and household goods to fund cancer programs, open in Menlo Park since about 1981. In 1995 it moved from 746 Santa Cruz Avenue into the larger space next door at 748, where it is still open.

Family-run Italian restaurant that opened here in spring 1997 as Scala Mia, a second location of a Burlingame restaurant, and was later called Angelo Mio before becoming Roma Italian Cuisine. Still open.
Boba cafe, also called Mr. Green Bubble, serving milk tea, egg waffles and rice bowls. It opened in late summer 2019 and is still open.

Family barber shop that opened in 1940 in one of five small storefronts in a 1937 building on El Camino Real, a space first used by Pacific Greyhound Lines. Local historians say 49ers players got haircuts here while the team trained at Menlo College from 1946 to 1954.
Breakfast and lunch restaurant that opened on October 7, 2002, in a space that earlier held Koo Koo Roo and Fresh Choice. It was a local breakfast favorite by 2006 and is still open.
High-end rug gallery on Santa Cruz Avenue, opened in Menlo Park in 1991 after the owner's earlier store in Santa Fe. Still open today.
Furniture and interior-design showroom that opened in August 2013 in the former Traditions space on Santa Cruz Avenue. It is still open today.
Women's clothing boutique, the first Alys Grace store, opened in Menlo Park in 2008 by a husband-and-wife team. The owners later opened stores in Los Altos, San Francisco and San Ramon.
Casual Mexican restaurant serving tacos, burritos, tortas and pupusas, opened in the former Applewood 2-Go pizza space. It officially opened on August 4, 2018.
Boba tea shop that opened in early 2020 in the former Cobblery shoe-repair space at El Camino Real and Menlo Avenue.
Running shoe store that opened in fall 2008, when new owners bought The Runner's High at this address and renamed it Fleet Feet. Still open today.
Korean-Taiwanese restaurant from the chefs behind Palo Alto's Maum. It opened in June 2025 and is still operating.
Women's clothing boutique on Santa Cruz Avenue, founded around 2009 and still open at this address.
Cocktail bar, also called Bar Loretta, run alongside the French restaurant Bistro Vida next door; it opened in February 2025 in the former Magoo's Pizza Parlor space and was still open in 2026.
Barre fitness studio at the corner of El Camino Real and Menlo Avenue, opened February 28, 2016. It closed in July 2020 and reopened under a new local franchisee in 2021.
Camera store that took over the former Ritz Camera shop on Santa Cruz Avenue in late 2012, when Colorado-based Mike's Camera bought it and renamed it. It is still open.
Italian restaurant (La Stanza Cucina Italiana), reported to have opened in January 2020 and still operating.

Home furnishings store run by the San Francisco retailer Anthem, next door to its Bed & Bath shop at 887 Santa Cruz Ave. Anthem says its downtown Menlo Park location opened in 2017, and the store is still open.

French bistro that opened on Santa Cruz Avenue in 1998 and was reportedly the street's first restaurant with full sidewalk service. It is still open, and the neighboring Bar Loretta was added in 2024.

Independent bookstore founded by Roy Kepler in 1955 at 939 El Camino Real, which moved to this Menlo Center location in 1989. It closed briefly in 2005, reopened within weeks with community backing, and is still open today.

fields.name: Amici's East Coast Pizzeria
fields.note: East Coast-style pizzeria that opened in May 2009 in the former Dal Baffo restaurant space. It is still open today.
Kitchen and bath design showroom that opened on Santa Cruz Avenue in 2013 and marked its 10th anniversary in June 2023. It is still open.
Women's clothing, textiles and handicrafts shop that opened around 2004 as Dolma's first store and is still open. The brand now also has stores in Palo Alto and San Francisco.
Seafood restaurant that opened on April 22, 2025, in the space Ann's Coffee Shop held for 75 years until it closed in 2021.
Middle Eastern dessert bakery and cafe, also known as LeVant Dessert, that soft-opened in January 2024 and held its grand opening that February. It was still operating in 2025.
Hair salon founded in 2021, according to the salon's own website and a gift-card listing. It is still open at 812 Santa Cruz Ave.
Opened in 2012 as Lyna's Skin Care and later grew into a full beauty salon and nail spa, according to a gift-card listing. It is still open at 515 El Camino Real.
Hair salon on El Camino Real, open in Menlo Park by mid-2025 and still operating.
Jenny Craig weight-loss center on El Camino Real, listed in business directories at 811 El Camino Real. It closed in May 2023 when the chain shut all its locations; the year it opened isn't known.
Martial arts and self-defense studio, open at this address since at least August 1994 and still open today. The exact opening year isn't known.
Singaporean restaurant on Chestnut Street from 1999 until the building was sold and tenants had to leave by January 1, 2025. It later reopened at 625 Oak Grove Ave.
Italian restaurant near El Camino Real and Santa Cruz Avenue, opened around 2001 according to a 2006 local newspaper profile. It is still open today.
Dim sum restaurant that opened on January 29, 2017, in the space of the former sit-down Su Hong restaurant, which had been there since 1977. Its owner also ran the Su Hong to-go location nearby.
Cafe from a Truckee-based coffee company, its first location outside the Tahoe area. It soft-opened on January 10, 2018, in a space that had housed Nak's Oriental Market and Absolutely Nails.

Beverage and liquor store in the El Camino Real shopping center shared with Staples, in a space that once held a Chili's restaurant. The city approved it in November 2010 after a contested permit process, and it opened around early 2011.
Malaysian restaurant that opened in March 2017 in the former Menlo Hub space. It closed during the pandemic in 2020, and The Mandarin later took over the space.

City Hall moved in 1948 to the newly bought former Dibble Hospital land, which became the Laurel Street civic center. Staff first worked in temporary and former hospital buildings, and City Hall is still on this campus today.
Office-supply store that opened on October 9, 2004 in space formerly occupied by Strouds Fine Linens. It is still open in the El Camino Real shopping center it shares with BevMo!
Philz Coffee opened on May 10, 2021 in the new building at Santa Cruz Avenue and Merrill Street, across from the Caltrain station. It is still open today.
Longtime used bookstore that moved here from El Camino Real in 2021 after its original building was demolished. It is still open today.
Family-owned toy store that opened in November 1999 at 714 Santa Cruz Ave and moved to this larger space around 2007. The current owners bought it in 2002, and it is still open.
Pet supply store and grooming shop at 654 Santa Cruz Ave, open today. The year it opened has not been confirmed.
Ace-affiliated hardware store that opened in August 2005 in the front of the longtime Menlo Park Hardware building, which had closed in 2001. It is still open today.
Italian restaurant that opened in 1988 and became one of downtown Menlo Park's longest-running restaurants. It closed on June 22, 2025, after about 36 years.
Bakery selling naturally leavened bread and pastries. It started as a pop-up and opened this permanent shop next to Philz Coffee in early March 2022.
Barbershop and hair salon on Chestnut Street; its owner says it opened in 1974. In 2016 barbers from the closing Golden Shears moved here.
Brunch restaurant with floral decor on Merrill Street near Oak Grove Ave, close to the Caltrain station. It was open by late 2021 and is still listed at this address.
Thai restaurant across from the Menlo Park Caltrain station. It is a branch of a San Francisco restaurant and opened in fall 2020, shortly after San Mateo County allowed indoor dining again.
Coffee shop run by the chef behind Camper, inside the CANOPY space in the Springline development. It opened on November 1, 2022 as the development's first food business.
Hair salon that the salon's own website says had its grand opening in 2019. It is still open, and a current listing places it at 1148 Crane St.
Jewelry shop with a showroom on Crane Street. The business was founded in 2019, but the year the showroom opened at this address is approximate.

fields.name: Canteen
fields.note: Wine, cocktail and tapas bar in the Springline development, opened on January 25, 2023. It was the development's first closure and shut permanently on December 14, 2024.
Brewery taproom and kitchen in the Springline development, opened in summer 2023 in Suite B. It is still open today.
The San Francisco roaster opened its first cafe outside the city in 2023, in the Springline development. It serves coffee and pastries and is still open.

Restaurant and bar in the 1920s bank building at El Camino Real and Santa Cruz Avenue, which later served as Menlo Park's city hall. It opened in 1977, closed for remodeling in 2012 and reopened in December 2016 with its entrance moved to Santa Cruz Avenue.
Burma Love, a Burmese restaurant from San Francisco, opened in the Springline development in July 2023. It is still open.
Grab-and-go food shop in the Springline development, which local press said would open in May 2023. A 2024 listing shows it still operating at this address.
Omakase sushi restaurant from San Francisco's Robin, in the Springline development. It opened on September 21, 2023, during Springline's grand opening, and is still open.
Italian restaurant from San Francisco's Che Fico in the Springline development. It opened on November 8, 2023, and is still open.
Optical store in the Menlo Station shopping center on El Camino Real. Its state optical-dispensing license at this address dates to 1987, and it is still open.

Mongolian barbecue restaurant on El Camino Real, between the CVS and BevMo!, where diners choose their own ingredients to be cooked. It opened in June 2012 in a space that had held the Deeelish catering company.
Uyghur restaurant run by two sisters, which soft-opened in December 2022. It closed in September 2026, and the space reopened in October 2026 as Dragon General, a Chinese restaurant.
Restaurant known for heritage-breed chicken and aged wines, with the Somm Cellars wine shop next door. It opened Oct. 28, 2025, in the former Le Boulanger space.

fields.name: Il Mercato di Che Fico
fields.note: Italian market in the Springline development, next to Che Fico Parco Menlo, selling housemade pasta, gelato, prepared foods and produce. It opened on March 21, 2024, and closed for good on April 19, 2025.
Cafe from the team behind Little Sky Bakery on Santa Cruz Avenue. It was a farmers' market favorite before opening this permanent spot around 2024, and press that year described it as new.
Massage therapy clinic that applied in 2024 for a city use permit to convert a former retail space, and opened around 2025.
Cal-Indian restaurant from the team behind Ettan. It opened in January 2025 at The Villa Menlo Park in Stanford's Middle Plaza development.

Turkish and Mediterranean restaurant near El Camino Real and Santa Cruz Avenue, established in 2006 according to the restaurant itself. A Palo Alto Online review published June 30, 2006 already lists it at 1149 El Camino Real, and it remains open daily.
Menlo Park's main public library opened in 1957 in a new single-story building at the Laurel Street civic center, after voters approved a bond in 1956. The city still runs its main library here.

The congregation was founded in 1873 and met at 700 Santa Cruz Avenue for 76 years before moving to this Santa Cruz Avenue campus at Johnson Street in 1950. It is still active here today and is now known as Menlo Church.

Family supermarket that Frank Draeger opened around 1955 near Santa Cruz Avenue and University Drive, six years after the family's first store in San Mateo. It was expanded around 1990 and is still open today.

Chinese takeout restaurant that took the Chef Kwan's name in fall 2015, when new owner Jason Kwan bought Su Hong To Go, which had been at this address since 1991. It kept the Su Hong menu and is still open today.
Retro diner-style hamburger restaurant that opened in fall 2007 in the former Henry's Steak House space on El Camino Real. Still open today.

City recreation center on the civic center campus that offers classes and rentable meeting rooms. It was renovated with donations from developer John Arrillaga and has carried his family's name since about 2011.

corrections.target: Oak Grove Station Menlo Park Post Office

fields.note: Menlo Park's post office moved into this building in 1961, after earlier locations including 560 Oak Grove Ave. It became a branch, Oak Grove Station, once the Bohannon Drive post office opened in 1962, and it is still open.
Opened in 1926 as the Menlo Theatre and was renamed the Guild in the late 1940s. It stopped showing films in 2019 and reopened in 2022 as a live music venue.
Family-owned leather and fabric furniture showroom, open at this address since 2003 according to the business.

First Republic Bank branch near Oak Grove Avenue; building permits for its sign and remodel were issued in late 1997. The bank failed in May 2023, and city records later describe the building as a vacant former bank.
Hotel on El Camino Real in downtown Menlo Park, in a building dating from 1962. A 2019 Palo Alto Online list of long-running local businesses dates the inn to 1962, and it is still open.
Auto repair shop on El Camino Real that says it has been in business since 1968. San Mateo County lists it at this address as a used motor oil drop-off site.

fields.name: Naomi Sushi
fields.note: Japanese sushi restaurant on El Camino Real that opened in fall 1997, first under the name Naomi Sushi Pasta Grill. It closed abruptly in July 2024 for what a door notice called renovations, and has not been reported as reopening.
Breakfast and lunch cafe that opened on El Camino Real in 2008 and closed in May 2019. It reopened at the same address in 2023.
Store selling back-care products and ergonomic furniture on El Camino Real. A local shopping column listed it at this address in May 1995, and it still operates there.
A model railroad club founded in 1947. It has been in the former Railway Express Agency depot at the Menlo Park train station since 1950, and it holds free public open houses there.
Convenience store that was already open by June 2002, when a fire badly damaged it and a Chinese restaurant in the same building. It is still open at this address.

The parish's 1886 chapel was moved to Pine Street near Ravenswood Avenue in 1947, and a new church was built on Ravenswood at Laurel Street in 1957. The church is still active here and now calls itself Trinity Church in Menlo Park.
Japanese izakaya known for sake and charcoal-grilled yakitori, opened October 1, 2023 in the former Gombei restaurant space. Still open.
Hawaiian plate-lunch restaurant, listed at this address in a March 2005 Metro guide and still open today; its exact opening year is unknown.
Shipping, printing and mailbox store (The UPS Store #865), open today at 405 El Camino Real. The year it opened isn't known yet.

The first Round Table Pizza opened on December 21, 1959, at 1235 El Camino Real in a former water company building. After 1978 the founder rebuilt one door down at 1225 El Camino Real, where the restaurant is still open.

Supermarket listed at this El Camino Real location in the 1955 city directory; Safeway had been in Menlo Park since at least 1937 at 1137 El Camino Real. The original store was later torn down and replaced with a new building, and it is still open.

corrections.target: Nativity of the Holy Virgin Orthodox Church

fields.note: The 1886 chapel, originally Holy Trinity Episcopal Church, was given to the Orthodox parish, moved to Crane Street in October 1957 and consecrated in May 1958. The church is still active here.

City-run gymnastics center at Burgess Park on the civic center campus, paid for with donations from developer John Arrillaga's family. It held its grand opening on May 11, 2012, and reopened in February 2026 after storm flooding closed it.
61-room boutique hotel on El Camino Real that opened in late September 2018, with the Oak + Violet restaurant opening inside in October. It is still operating.
Outdoor coffee kiosk from the San Francisco roaster, across from the Menlo Park Caltrain station. It opened on August 19, 2019 as a required public benefit of the Alma Station office development.
